text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Electricity Supply Commission of Malawi said on Thursday that according to an internal audit report its employee Edward Mlongoti, who stands as the main opposition Malawi Congress Party candidate in the November 19 by-election in Blantyre, was dishonest and had misappropriated funds.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party may not contest in the November 19 by-election in Blantyre after its candidate, Edward Mlongoti was reportedly joining the ruling United Democratic Front party if he withdraws from the race to be compensated with an executive post at ESCOM where he is employed as a meter reader.

- Police fired in the air at minister of information Brown Mpinganjira's house in Blantyre on Thursday when main opposition Malawi Congress Party supporters tried to track the party's candidate in the November 19 by-election, Edward Mlongoti, who was reported missing the whole day.

- Two opposition parties MCP and Alliance for Democracy and the Malawi Institute of Democratic and Economic Affairs condemned the ruling UDF party for refusing to attend mediated talks to resolve the current standstill in parliament.
- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party's candidate in the November 19 by-election in Blantyre faces possible arrest on grounds of fraud.
- More than 40 female patients in Mwanza, more than 100km east of Blantyre, fled in panic on Tuesday night when an owl invaded their ward at about 2300 local time.
